analyzed_vuln.description: The crash is caused by calling the specialized SP-math point-add routine with invalid/uninitialized projective point data and without validating conversion success. In sp_ecc_proj_add_point_256(), inputs are converted via sp_256_from_mp(...) but return values are ignored, then sp_256_proj_point_add_5(p, p, q, tmp) is called unconditionally. With malformed fuzzed ECC point inputs (propagated from ecc_projective_add_point), this leads to wild memory reads inside sp_256_proj_point_add_5 and ASan SEGV.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: cryptofuzz OpECC_Point_Add -> ecc_projective_add_point() -> SP fast path for 256-bit modulus -> sp_ecc_proj_add_point_256() -> sp_256_proj_point_add_5(). Trigger requires the SP-math/public add path to be enabled and attacker-controlled ECC point coordinates that are not properly constrained for the SP representation. Because the SP wrapper does not check conversion/validity before invoking the low-level add primitive, crafted input can produce invalid internal state and crash on read in sp_256_proj_point_add_5.
